chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Hariz from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far or from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them) said:
Regarding the wife whom her husband has not had sexual intercourse with, he said: 'Ila' (oath of abstention) and Dhahr (formal divorce) do not apply to her.'

key_terms.إِيلَاءٌ: Ila: An oath by a husband to abstain from sexual intercourse with his wife for a specified period.
key_terms.ظِهَارٌ: Dhahr: A pre-Islamic form of divorce where a husband compares his wife's back to the back of his mother, rendering her unlawful until expiation.

ai.seo_question: Do Ila and Dhahr apply to a wife before consummation?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies that the specific legal mechanisms of 'Ila' (oath of abstention) and 'Dhahr' (formal declaration of separation) are inapplicable to a wife whose husband has not yet consummated the marriage, as these rulings presuppose an established marital bond with sexual relations. This distinction is crucial in Shia jurisprudence for determining the correct procedure for divorce or separation in cases of non-consummation, differentiating it from the more complex rulings applied after consummation.
